resolution: Follow-up audit: tallied EVERY fixed wall bounding what can be built. GPU: 256 MiB geometry buffer (112 MiB retained unique meshes = 3.67M verts + 144 MiB dyn tail), 32 MiB static instance pool (1,048,576 placed pieces), 24 MiB slim foliage pool, 2,048 interned shapes, 32,768 scene meshes — ~360 MiB total fixed budget. Physics: 16,384 rect + 16,384 oriented colliders, 256 heightfields, 128 entities. Map: 1,377-chunk address space (18.4km x 1.1km), 64-chunk live paint mirror, ~640 KB CPU per painted chunk (on-demand, unbounded). Root finding: gpu.zig passes NULL device limits so the whole stack sits under WebGPU's DEFAULT 256 MiB maxBufferSize — a default nobody chose, not VRAM. Reported to user with the counterweight that instancing multiplies buildable world beyond raw MB (Vice City pattern). Awaiting the user's elastic-pools + real-device-limits ruling (req_2839/2840/2841 all point at it); no code changed.
